title: PulseGrid: Wayfinding redistribution and compact workspace switching
creator: Asha Menon
description: Rework the Console information architecture to reduce cognitive load for multi-tenant users and introduce a compact, keyboard-first workspace switcher. Deliver high-fidelity prototypes for left-rail redistribution (top-level clusters: Activity, Models, Deployments, Cost & Billing, Observability), a contextual secondary rail for per-workspace actions, and a low-friction workspace switch flow that supports instant previews and pinned favorites.
acceptance_criteria: Top-level navigation re-clustered into 5 consistent zones and validated with two rounds of moderated usability tests (n=8 each) with PM/Platform personas.
Compact workspace switcher prototype supports keyboard open (Cmd/Ctrl+K), fuzzy search, recent-workspaces, and pin/unpin actions; 80% of test tasks completed without instructor prompts.

Cost & Billing moved into a first-class cluster with a persistent cost lens panel accessible from any route; panel prototype demonstrates token-level cost breakdowns and quick switch to per-route filters.
Left-rail collapsible state persisted per-user, with clear affordance for compact vs expanded layout (A11Y contrast and screenreader announcements in prototype).
Design handoff artifacts (Figma components, interaction specs) delivered with tokenized spacing and responsive rules for 3 breakpoints and an engineering JIRA/ENG dependency outlined.
Rollout plan documented with canary cohort, telemetry events to measure time-to-switch, nav clicks, and cost-panel usage.
Performance guardrails: prototypes demonstrate <= 120ms perceived response for workspace switch animation in 90th percentile using mocked data in InVision microbenchmarks.
design_notes: PulseGrid is a naming umbrella for the redistributed IA — aim is to reduce discovery steps by grouping related workflows (eg. Rollouts, Canary, A/B in Deployments cluster).

Prototype 1 (vertical clusters): shows heavy affordances for Cost & Billing with inline sparklines and a persistent cost toggle. Prototype 2 (tabbed clusters): reduces vertical density; used for A/B testing.
Micro-interactions: introduce a rapid preview overlay when hovering a workspace chip showing active model, region, and last 5 deploys. Keep overlay non-blocking and keyboard-focusable.

Accessibility: keyboard focus order must map to nav clustering; implement aria-expanded semantics for collapsible rail and aria-live region for workspace switch confirmation. Color token palette adjusted to meet 4.5:1 contrast for interactive states.
Prototyping tech: Figma interactive components + Loom walkthroughs for PM/Eng review. Use lightweight HTML/CSS prototype for perceived latency tests.
decisions: Favor vertical clustering over nested menus to reduce click depth; clusters are sticky and user-customizable in later iterations.
Compact mode will hide labels and keep icons + numeric badges; users can toggle with a persistent keyboard shortcut and preference setting.
Workspace switching will be modal by default on small screens but instantaneous overlay on desktop to preserve context. Modal uses a stepping transition for perceived speed.
Cost lens is surfaceable from every route via a dedicated chip in the cluster header; not gated behind a separate settings page to improve discoverability for cost-sensitive customers.
